3: //! Signal driver
4: 
5: use crate::io::driver::{Driver as IoDriver, Interest, Ready, TOKEN_WAKEUP};
6: use crate::io::PollEvented;
7: use crate::park::Park;
8: use crate::signal::registry::globals;
9: 
10: use mio::net::UnixStream;
11: use std::io::{self, Read};
12: use std::ptr;
13: use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};
14: use std::task::{Context, Poll, RawWaker, RawWakerVTable, Waker};
15: use std::time::Duration;
16: 
17: /// Responsible for registering wakeups when an OS signal is received, and
18: /// subsequently dispatching notifications to any signal listeners as appropriate.
19: ///
20: /// Note: this driver relies on having an enabled IO driver in order to listen to
21: /// pipe write wakeups.
22: #[derive(Debug)]
23: pub(crate) struct Driver {
24:     /// Thread parker. The `Driver` park implementation delegates to this.
25:     park: IoDriver,
26: 
27:     /// A pipe for receiving wake events from the signal handler
28:     receiver: PollEvented<UnixStream>,
29: 
30:     /// Shared state
31:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
32: }
33: 
34: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
35: pub(crate) struct Handle {
36:     inner: Weak<Inner>,
37: }
38: 
39: #[derive(Debug)]
40: pub(super) struct Inner(());
41: 
42: // ===== impl Driver =====
43: 
44: impl Driver {
45:     /// Creates a new signal `Driver` instance that delegates wakeups to `park`.
46:     pub(crate) fn new(park: IoDriver) -> io::Result<Self> {
47:         use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
48:         use std::os::unix::io::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
49: 
50:         // NB: We give each driver a "fresh" receiver file descriptor to avoid
51:         // the issues described in alexcrichton/tokio-process#42.
52:         //
53:         // In the past we would reuse the actual receiver file descriptor and
54:         // swallow any errors around double registration of the same descriptor.
55:         // I'm not sure if the second (failed) registration simply doesn't end
56:         // up receiving wake up notifications, or there could be some race
57:         // condition when consuming readiness events, but having distinct
58:         // descriptors for distinct PollEvented instances appears to mitigate
59:         // this.
60:         //
61:         // Unfortunately we cannot just use a single global PollEvented instance
62:         // either, since we can't compare Handles or assume they will always
63:         // point to the exact same reactor.
64:         //
65:         // Mio 0.7 removed `try_clone()` as an API due to unexpected behavior
66:         // with registering dups with the same reactor. In this case, duping is
67:         // safe as each dup is registered with separate reactors **and** we
68:         // only expect at least one dup to receive the notification.
69: 
70:         // Manually drop as we don't actually own this instance of UnixStream.
71:         let receiver_fd = globals().receiver.as_raw_fd();
72: 
73:         // safety: there is nothing unsafe about this, but the `from_raw_fd` fn is marked as unsafe.
74:         let original =
75:             ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::from_raw_fd(receiver_fd) });
76:         let receiver = UnixStream::from_std(original.try_clone()?);
77:         let receiver = PollEvented::new_with_interest_and_handle(
78:             receiver,
79:             Interest::READABLE | Interest::WRITABLE,
80:             park.handle(),
81:         )?;
82: 
83:         Ok(Self {
84:             park,
85:             receiver,
86:             inner: Arc::new(Inner(())),
87:         })
88:     }
89: 
90:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
91:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.
92:     pub(crate) fn handle(&self) -> Handle {
93:         Handle {
94:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     fn turn(&mut self, max_wait: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<()> {
99:         // How often to call `compact()` on the resource slab
100:         const COMPACT_INTERVAL: u8 = 255;
101: 
102:         self.park.tick = self.park.tick.wrapping_add(1);
103: 
104:         if self.park.tick == COMPACT_INTERVAL {
105:             self.park.resources.compact()
106:         }
107: 
108:         let mut events = self
109:             .park
110:             .events
111:             .take()
112:             .expect("i/o driver event store missing");
113: 
114:         // Block waiting for an event to happen, peeling out how many events
115:         // happened.
116:         match self.park.poll.poll(&mut events, max_wait) {
117:             Ok(_) => {}
118:             Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => {}
119:             #[cfg(tokio_wasi)]
120:             Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput => {
121:                 // In case of wasm32_wasi this error happens, when trying to poll without subscriptions
122:                 // just return from the park, as there would be nothing, which wakes us up.
123:             }
124:             Err(e) => return Err(e),
125:         }
126: 
127:         // Process all the events that came in, dispatching appropriately
128:         let mut ready_count = 0;
129:         for event in events.iter() {
130:             let token = event.token();
131: 
132:             if token != TOKEN_WAKEUP {
133:                 self.park.dispatch(token, Ready::from_mio(event));
134:                 ready_count += 1;
135:             }
136:         }
137: 
138:         self.park.inner.metrics.incr_ready_count_by(ready_count);
139: 
140:         self.park.events = Some(events);
141: 
142:         Self::process(&self.receiver);
143:         Ok(())
144:     }
145: 
146:     fn process(receiver: &PollEvented<UnixStream>) {
147:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
148:         //
149:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
150:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
151:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
152:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
153: 
154:         let ev = match receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
155:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
156:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
157:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
158:         };
159: 
160:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
161:         // if another signal has come in.
162:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
163:         loop {
164:             match (&**receiver).read(&mut buf) {
165:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
166:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
167:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
168:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
169:             }
170:         }
171: 
172:         receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
173: 
174:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
175:         globals().broadcast();
176:     }
177: }
178: 
179: const NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE: RawWakerVTable = RawWakerVTable::new(noop_clone, noop, noop, noop);
180: 
181: unsafe fn noop_clone(_data: *const ()) -> RawWaker {
182:     RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)
183: }
184: 
185: unsafe fn noop(_data: *const ()) {}
186: 
187: // ===== impl Park for Driver =====
188: 
189: impl Park for Driver {
190:     type Unpark = <IoDriver as Park>::Unpark;
191:     type Error = io::Error;
192: 
193:     fn unpark(&self) -> Self::Unpark {
194:         self.park.unpark()
195:     }
196: 
197:     fn park(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
198:         self.turn(None)?;
199:         Ok(())
200:     }
201: 
202:     fn park_timeout(&mut self, duration: Duration) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
203:         self.turn(Some(duration))?;
204:         Ok(())
205:     }
206: 
207:     fn shutdown(&mut self) {
208:         self.park.shutdown()
209:     }
210: }
211: 
212: // ===== impl Handle =====
213: 
214: impl Handle {
215:     pub(super) fn check_inner(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
216:         if self.inner.strong_count() > 0 {
217:             Ok(())
218:         } else {
219:             Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Other, "signal driver gone"))
220:         }
221:     }
222: }
223: 
224: cfg_rt! {
225:     impl Handle {
226:         /// Returns a handle to the current driver
227:         ///
228:         /// # Panics
229:         ///
230:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
231:         #[track_caller]
232:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
233:             crate::runtime::context::signal_handle().expect(
234:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime",
235:             )
236:         }
237:     }
238: }
239:

243:         ///
244:         /// # Panics
245:         ///
246:         /// This function panics if there is no current signal driver set.
247:         #[track_caller]
248:         pub(super) fn current() -> Self {
249:             panic!(
250:                 "there is no signal driver running, must be called from the context of Tokio runtime or with\
251:                 `rt` enabled.",
252:             )
253:         }
254:     }
255: }

part.text:
Confirmed pre-existing failure, unrelated to the fix.

**Fix applied**: `tokio/src/signal/unix/driver.rs:79` — removed `Interest::WRITABLE` from the signal receiver registration, keeping only `Interest::READABLE`. Since the driver never writes to the self-pipe, the writable interest was pointless and (with level-triggered selectors) causes an infinite readiness spin.

Verification: all signal tests (`signal`, `signal_drop_rt`, `signal_drop_signal`, `signal_multi_rt`, `signal_no_rt`, `signal_notify_both`, `signal_panic`, `signal_twice`, `signal_usr1`) and the full `cargo test -p tokio --features full` suite pass; the only failure (`macros_join::join_size`) pre-exists on the untouched tree.
